title: Trees Are So Weird

blocks.en_text: Every tree you have ever seen is dead.
blocks.zh_text: 你见过的每一棵树，其实都是死的。

blocks.en_text: It turns out the alive part of a tree is  just a tiny, paper thin strip of cells,
blocks.zh_text: 原来，一棵树活着的部分，只是一小条薄如纸的细胞层，

blocks.en_text: trapped between a dead skeleton and dead outsides.
blocks.zh_text: 夹在死掉的骨架和死掉的外层之间。

blocks.en_text: Trees are some of the most extreme beings on  earth with one of the most unique strategies in
blocks.zh_text: 树木是地球上最极端的生物之一，拥有自然界最独特的生存策略之一——

blocks.en_text: nature – on top of being mostly dead stuff, they  forge their body out of thin air, they mercilessly
blocks.zh_text: 除了大部分都是死掉的东西之外，它们还能凭空造出自己的身躯，它们会毫不留情地

blocks.en_text: crush rocks with acid, and they have an internal  negative pressure that would kill you instantly.
blocks.zh_text: 用酸腐蚀岩石，而且它们体内有一种负压，能瞬间要了你的命。

blocks.en_text: So, how do trees actually work?
blocks.zh_text: 那么，树木到底是怎么运作的呢？

blocks.en_text: Let’s go back…to the beginning.
blocks.zh_text: 让我们回到……最初的时候。

blocks.en_text: The Ancient Battle for the Sky
blocks.zh_text: 远古的天空争夺战

blocks.en_text: For over a billion years the ancestors
blocks.zh_text: 在超过十亿年的时间里，植物的祖先

blocks.en_text: of plants only inhabited the sun  drenched surfaces of the oceans.
blocks.zh_text: 只生活在阳光充足的海洋表面。

blocks.en_text: Their bodies were thin and delicate  and absorbed water straight through
blocks.zh_text: 它们的身体又薄又脆弱，直接通过

blocks.en_text: their surfaces, getting their  energy through photosynthesis.
blocks.zh_text: 表面吸收水分，靠光合作用获取能量。

blocks.en_text: Forging sunlight, carbon  dioxide and water into sugar.
blocks.zh_text: 把阳光、二氧化碳和水转化成糖。

blocks.en_text: But about 470 million years ago they decided  to conquer a hostile alien planet: the land.
blocks.zh_text: 但大约4.7亿年前，它们决定征服一个充满敌意的外星世界：陆地。

blocks.en_text: Like green rugs with ambition these  plant ancestors began clinging to
blocks.zh_text: 这些植物祖先就像野心勃勃的绿色地毯，开始紧紧贴附在

blocks.en_text: the ground wherever it was wet and damp.
blocks.zh_text: 任何潮湿的地方。

blocks.en_text: But now, with solid ground beneath  and no ability to float around a new
blocks.zh_text: 但现在，脚下有了坚实的地面，又没法四处漂浮，一个新的

blocks.en_text: dimension became a place of intense warfare: up.
blocks.zh_text: 维度变成了激烈厮杀的战场：向上。

blocks.en_text: The higher they grew, the more sun they would  get, while starving their competition below.
blocks.zh_text: 它们长得越高，得到的阳光就越多，同时让下面的竞争对手挨饿。

blocks.en_text: Height became a deadly weapon.  The battle for the sky had begun.
blocks.zh_text: 高度成了一种致命武器。天空争夺战就此打响。

blocks.en_text: Until now, plants were built mostly from  cellulose, which was great for shape,
blocks.zh_text: 在此之前，植物主要由纤维素构成，这对塑造形状很有利，

blocks.en_text: but not for strength, which  limited how tall they could grow.
blocks.zh_text: 但对强度没什么帮助，这就限制了它们能长多高。

blocks.en_text: Over dozens of millions of  years of evolutionary warfare,
blocks.zh_text: 经过数千万年的进化战争，

blocks.en_text: a group of plants developed one of  life's greatest breakthroughs: lignin.
blocks.zh_text: 有一类植物发展出了生命最伟大的突破之一：木质素。

blocks.en_text: Lignin is a macromolecule made  of ring-shaped structures.
blocks.zh_text: 木质素是一种由环状结构构成的大分子。

blocks.en_text: It is rigid, tough, waterproof,  and incredibly hard to break down.
blocks.zh_text: 它坚硬、强韧、防水，而且极难分解。

blocks.en_text: Concrete in a world made of jelly.
blocks.zh_text: 就像果冻世界里的混凝土。

blocks.en_text: It filled gaps between cellulose threads,  stiffening and locking everything into place.
blocks.zh_text: 它填满纤维素丝之间的空隙，把一切加固并锁定到位。

blocks.en_text: Lignin gave plants the strength to grow  taller and claim the sun for themselves.
blocks.zh_text: 木质素赋予了植物长高的力量，让它们把阳光据为己有。

blocks.en_text: But of course now they were  competing with each other,
blocks.zh_text: 但当然，现在它们开始互相竞争了，

blocks.en_text: which must have been really annoying for them.
blocks.zh_text: 这对它们来说肯定特别烦人。

blocks.en_text: So as more millions of years passed,  some plants just went all in on lignin
blocks.zh_text: 所以又过了数百万年，有些植物干脆全力投入木质素

blocks.en_text: and produced more and more of it,  becoming stiffer, harder and stronger.
blocks.zh_text: 并制造出越来越多的木质素，变得越来越坚硬、结实、强壮。

blocks.en_text: Until one day, around 385 million years ago they
blocks.zh_text: 直到有一天，大约3.85亿年前，它们

blocks.en_text: got the biological equivalent of  steel reinforced concrete: wood.
blocks.zh_text: 获得了生物学上相当于钢筋混凝土的东西：木材。

blocks.en_text: More on it later, but with this magic  material the first trees emerged.
blocks.zh_text: 这个稍后再细说，但凭借这种神奇的材料，最早的树木出现了。

blocks.en_text: Almost immediately they became  the largest living beings alive,
blocks.zh_text: 几乎立刻，它们就成了当时最大的生物，

blocks.en_text: shooting up to 20 meters high into the  sky – and they only got bigger from here.
blocks.zh_text: 蹿升到20米高，直插天空——而且从此以后它们只会越来越大。

blocks.en_text: But this enormous size created  extremely hard problems:
blocks.zh_text: 但这种巨大的体型带来了极其棘手的难题：

blocks.en_text: How do you get water from the ground up to the  green parts that do the actual photosynthesis?
blocks.zh_text: 你怎么把水从地面运到上面那些真正进行光合作用的绿色部分？

blocks.en_text: And how do you get the sugar they produce  down to the cells that keep you up there?
blocks.zh_text: 又怎么把它们制造的糖分往下运到那些支撑你高高在上的细胞？

blocks.en_text: On the scale of a cell a distance of  a few meters is like you’re working
blocks.zh_text: 在细胞的尺度上，几米的距离就像你在

blocks.en_text: in Britain while your lunch box is  in Egypt and your drink in New York.
blocks.zh_text: 英国工作，而你的饭盒在埃及，你的饮料在纽约。

blocks.en_text: How do you not die?
blocks.zh_text: 你怎么才能不死？

blocks.en_text: So trees came up with one of the  most amazing ways any organism grows,
blocks.zh_text: 于是树木想出了任何生物生长方式中最了不起的一种，

blocks.en_text: and became nearly immortal by accident.
blocks.zh_text: 并且意外地变得几乎永生不死。

blocks.en_text: A Conveyor Belt of Death
blocks.zh_text: 一条死亡传送带

blocks.en_text: Let us slice an ancient tree in half  and get to the heart running it all:
blocks.zh_text: 让我们把一棵古树切成两半，深入它的核心，看看是什么在运转这一切：

blocks.en_text: the cambium, a razor-thin, circular  zone, just a few stem cells wide.
blocks.zh_text: 形成层，一个薄如刀片的环状区域，只有几个干细胞那么宽。

blocks.en_text: These stem cells grow inward and outwards,  turning into two groups of specialists.
blocks.zh_text: 这些干细胞向内和向外生长，变成两组专职细胞。

blocks.en_text: The inward specialists are on a  conveyor belt of death, the xylem.
blocks.zh_text: 向内的专职细胞处在一条死亡传送带上，那就是木质部。

blocks.en_text: With each new division it is  pushing the cambium outwards,
blocks.zh_text: 每分裂一次，它就把形成层往外推，

blocks.en_text: making the tree thicker the older it gets.
blocks.zh_text: 让树越老越粗。

blocks.en_text: As the xylem cells mature their  lignin production goes into overdrive,
blocks.zh_text: 随着木质部细胞成熟，它们的木质素生产进入超速状态，

blocks.en_text: and they become hard and stuffy, like  a muscle slowly transforming into bone.
blocks.zh_text: 变得又硬又密实，就像一块肌肉慢慢变成骨头。

blocks.en_text: They begin to hollow themselves out, shedding  everything that once made them alive.
blocks.zh_text: 它们开始把自己掏空，褪去一切曾经让它们活着的东西。

blocks.en_text: And then they die.
blocks.zh_text: 然后它们就死了。

blocks.en_text: What’s left is a corpse, a hard, empty tube.
blocks.zh_text: 剩下的是尸体，一根坚硬、空心的管子。

blocks.en_text: As the tree grows year after year, new  corpses are layered on old corpses,
blocks.zh_text: 随着树木年复一年地生长，新的尸体一层层叠在旧尸体上，

blocks.en_text: forming rings of hardened, dead tissue.
blocks.zh_text: 形成一圈圈硬化、死亡的组织。

blocks.en_text: A graveyard of trillions of plant bones.
blocks.zh_text: 一座埋葬着数万亿植物骨头的墓地。

blocks.en_text: This is what we call wood.
blocks.zh_text: 这就是我们所说的木材。

blocks.en_text: Stacked together they form a giant network of  pipes that stretches the whole length of the tree.
blocks.zh_text: 它们层层叠叠地连在一起，构成一个贯穿整棵树的大型管道网络。

blocks.en_text: This network uses the chemical properties of water
blocks.zh_text: 这个网络利用水的化学特性

blocks.en_text: and a few other tricks to move  it with incredible efficiency.
blocks.zh_text: 再加上一些其他窍门，以惊人的效率把水往上运。

blocks.en_text: Water molecules are, for a lack of a  better word, sticky, like tiny magnets,
blocks.zh_text: 水分子怎么说呢，很黏，就像小磁铁一样，

blocks.en_text: and naturally cling tightly to each other.
blocks.zh_text: 天然就会紧紧地吸附在一起。

blocks.en_text: When one moves, it pulls the next  along with it, like pulling on a rope.
blocks.zh_text: 一个分子移动时，会拉着下一个一起走，就像拉绳子一样。

blocks.en_text: In trees this rope starts in the roots and ends in  the leaves that bathe in the warmth from the sun.
blocks.zh_text: 在树里，这根绳子从根部开始，一直延伸到沐浴着阳光温暖的叶子里。

blocks.en_text: Here the heat from the sun evaporates 95% of
blocks.zh_text: 在这里，太阳的热量把95%的水蒸发掉，

blocks.en_text: the water that got sucked into the  roots, from billions of tiny pores,
blocks.zh_text: 这些水是被吸进根部的，从数十亿个微小的气孔中蒸发出去，

blocks.en_text: releasing a constant invisible mist of water  molecules around the crown of the tree.
blocks.zh_text: 在树冠周围不断释放出看不见的水分子雾气。

blocks.en_text: This process, called transpiration in plants,  creates tension on the rope of water molecules,
blocks.zh_text: 这个过程在植物中叫作蒸腾作用，它会在水分子组成的绳子上产生拉力，

blocks.en_text: stretching and lifting the entire column upwards,  all the way from the roots to the leaves.
blocks.zh_text: 把整根水柱往上拉、往上提，一路从根部送到叶子。

blocks.en_text: This pull is so insanely strong that  it can lift water over 100 meters,
blocks.zh_text: 这股拉力强得离谱，能把水提升到100多米高，

blocks.en_text: which requires sucking forces  equivalent to the pressure of
blocks.zh_text: 这需要的吸力相当于

blocks.en_text: dozens of atmospheres – as much as the crushing  pressure hundreds of meters deep in the ocean.
blocks.zh_text: 几十个大气压——跟海洋深处几百米处的巨大压力差不多。

blocks.en_text: Nothing humans have ever built  comes even close to this power.
blocks.zh_text: 人类造过的任何东西都远远比不上这种力量。

blocks.en_text: Even our best machines can’t pull  water higher than about 10 meters,
blocks.zh_text: 就连我们最好的机器，也只能把水抽到大约10米高，

blocks.en_text: because the negative pressure required  to pull hard enough makes it boil.
blocks.zh_text: 因为要抽得够用力所需的负压会让水沸腾。

blocks.en_text: But the water pipes of trees are so tiny  and narrow, almost perfectly airtight that
blocks.zh_text: 但树的水管又细又窄，几乎完全密封，所以

blocks.en_text: despite the insane suction pressure inside a  tree, water stays liquid and reaches the top.
blocks.zh_text: 尽管树内部的吸力大得惊人，水依然保持液态，一路到达顶端。

blocks.en_text: As the tree ages old xylem cells  eventually stop working and fill
blocks.zh_text: 随着树变老，老的木质部细胞最终会停止工作，

blocks.en_text: up with resins and other protective substances.
blocks.zh_text: 并被树脂和其他保护性物质填满。

blocks.en_text: Slowly they turn into heartwood, a dense,
blocks.zh_text: 它们慢慢变成心材，一个致密、

blocks.en_text: chemically fortified core that  is extremely resistant to decay.
blocks.zh_text: 经过化学加固的核心，极其耐腐。

blocks.en_text: The core of a mighty tree.
blocks.zh_text: 一棵参天大树的芯。

blocks.en_text: But water is only one half of the story.
blocks.zh_text: 但水只是故事的一半。

blocks.en_text: The sugar produced in the sky needs to be  transported to nourish cells down below.
blocks.zh_text: 在天空（叶子）中产生的糖分需要被运送下去，滋养下面的细胞。

blocks.en_text: And cells from the roots to  the leaves need to coordinate
blocks.zh_text: 而从根到叶的细胞需要相互协调，

blocks.en_text: and exchange information about damage and growth.
blocks.zh_text: 交换关于损伤和生长的信息。

blocks.en_text: This is the job of the cambium stem  cells that grow outwards: the phloem.
blocks.zh_text: 这是向外生长的形成层干细胞的工作：韧皮部。

blocks.en_text: The Tiny Living Part of the Tree
blocks.zh_text: 树中微小却活着的部分

blocks.en_text: As the Cells of the phloem  grow outwards they separate
blocks.zh_text: 随着韧皮部的细胞向外生长，它们分离开来

blocks.en_text: into three teams and make a brutal compromise.
blocks.zh_text: 分成三组，并达成一个残酷的妥协。

blocks.en_text: The first group are Sieve cells and their grim  fate is to become a living transport system.
blocks.zh_text: 第一组是筛胞，它们残酷的命运就是成为一套活着的运输系统。

blocks.en_text: Although “living” is not exactly right.
blocks.zh_text: 不过说“活着”其实不太准确。

blocks.en_text: As they mature they start to destroy themselves,
blocks.zh_text: 随着它们成熟，它们开始摧毁自己，

blocks.en_text: digest their organelles and even their  nuclei that houses their genetic code.
blocks.zh_text: 消化掉自己的细胞器，甚至消化掉装着遗传密码的细胞核。

blocks.en_text: At the same time they hollow themselves out,
blocks.zh_text: 与此同时，它们把自己掏空，

blocks.en_text: connecting to the sieve  cells above and below them.
blocks.zh_text: 与上下方的筛胞连接起来。

blocks.en_text: This goes on until they are a  sad shadow of living beings.
blocks.zh_text: 这一过程一直持续，直到它们沦为生命体可悲的影子。

blocks.en_text: A drooling, living tool without a brain  or arms, unable to support themselves.
blocks.zh_text: 一个流着口水的活工具，没有大脑也没有手臂，无法养活自己。

blocks.en_text: Only the second group, their  companion cells, keeps them alive.
blocks.zh_text: 只有第二组，也就是它们的伴胞，让它们活下去。

blocks.en_text: They connect with the crippled Sieve cells  via tiny channels and start maintaining them.
blocks.zh_text: 伴胞通过微小的通道与这些残缺的筛胞相连，开始维护它们，

blocks.en_text: Sending over energy, instructions  or repairing them if needed.
blocks.zh_text: 输送能量、指令，必要时还帮它们修复。

blocks.en_text: Running along the entire tree, these  two teams form a tiny and very thin
blocks.zh_text: 这两组细胞贯穿整棵树，形成一层微小而极薄的

blocks.en_text: layer of living sugar pipelines and signal  cables that stretch throughout the entire body.
blocks.zh_text: 活着的糖分管道和信号电缆，延伸至整个树身。

blocks.en_text: Providing food and information  wherever it is needed in the tree.
blocks.zh_text: 在树中任何需要的地方提供食物和信息。

blocks.en_text: The third team are Parenchyma cells, the silent
blocks.zh_text: 第三组是薄壁细胞，它们是树中沉默的

blocks.en_text: workers of the tree that are carrying  out essential labor in the background.
blocks.zh_text: 工人，在幕后承担着必不可少的工作。

blocks.en_text: Some are like mini pantries that store nutrients,
blocks.zh_text: 有些像小储藏室，储存养分、

blocks.en_text: sugars or water that the tree uses to survive  the winter, when it is unable to produce food.
blocks.zh_text: 糖分或水分，供树在冬天无法制造食物时维持生存。

blocks.en_text: Others are like mini healers that can  repair damage, while some go onto the
blocks.zh_text: 有些像小医生，能修复损伤，还有一些则转入

blocks.en_text: offensive and create toxins and anti  fungal bio weapons to kill intruders.
blocks.zh_text: 攻势，制造毒素和抗真菌生物武器来杀死入侵者。

blocks.en_text: On top of the phloem sits  another layer of stem cells.
blocks.zh_text: 在韧皮部之上还有另一层干细胞。

blocks.en_text: They are producing a second conveyor  belt of death, moving outside.
blocks.zh_text: 它们制造出第二条死亡传送带，向外延伸。

blocks.en_text: Special cells grow from this layer and as they  mature, just like the xylem cells in the center,
blocks.zh_text: 特殊的细胞从这一层长出来，当它们成熟时，就像中心的木质部细胞一样，

blocks.en_text: they kill themselves for the team,  turning into a hard guard wall – the bark.
blocks.zh_text: 它们为团队牺牲自己，变成一堵坚硬的防护墙——树皮。

blocks.en_text: Just like your skin, it protects the tiny living  layer from damage, parasites and invaders.
blocks.zh_text: 就像你的皮肤一样，它保护那层微小的活细胞免受损伤、寄生虫和入侵者的侵害。

blocks.en_text: So what is a tree?
blocks.zh_text: 那么，树到底是什么？

blocks.en_text: The living part of the stem is really  just this extremely thin and tiny layer,
blocks.zh_text: 茎的活体部分其实只是这极薄极小的一层，

blocks.en_text: a few millimeters thick, sitting on  a thick mountain of cell corpses,
blocks.zh_text: 只有几毫米厚，坐落在厚厚一堆细胞尸体之上，

blocks.en_text: surrounded by another layer of cell corpses.
blocks.zh_text: 外面又被另一层细胞尸体包围着。

blocks.en_text: The vast majority of the  biomass of a tree is dead.
blocks.zh_text: 一棵树绝大部分的生物量都是死的。

blocks.en_text: This is also why you really should not  damage the bark of trees because while
blocks.zh_text: 这也是为什么你真的不该去损伤树皮，因为虽然

blocks.en_text: it seems you are only doing a little damage, you  are actually killing the living part of the tree.
blocks.zh_text: 看起来你只是造成了一点小损伤，实际上你是在杀死树的活体部分。

blocks.en_text: But unless a tree is stopped by droughts,  diseases, storms or a human axe,
blocks.zh_text: 但除非一棵树被干旱、疾病、风暴或人类的斧头终结，

blocks.en_text: this system of being mostly dead kind  of makes trees potentially immortal.
blocks.zh_text: 这种大部分都是死的构造，反倒让树有可能长生不老。

blocks.en_text: They don’t age like we do, in principle  they could grow this way nearly forever.
blocks.zh_text: 它们不像我们那样衰老，原则上它们可以这样几乎永远生长下去。

blocks.en_text: Which is why we still have trees  around that were born when the
blocks.zh_text: 所以我们身边至今还有那些在

blocks.en_text: Egyptians started building their  first pyramid, 5000 years ago.
blocks.zh_text: 埃及人开始建造第一座金字塔时、也就是5000年前出生的树。

blocks.en_text: Really what kills a tree is the world around it.
blocks.zh_text: 真正杀死一棵树的，其实是它周围的世界。

blocks.en_text: Trees are not a real biological category but one  of the most successful ideas life has ever had,
blocks.zh_text: 树并不是一个真正的生物学分类，而是生命有过的最成功的点子之一，

blocks.en_text: and many different species developed on their own.
blocks.zh_text: 许多不同的物种各自独立演化出了这种形态。

blocks.en_text: These plants won the battle for the sky,  solved every challenge that had kept
blocks.zh_text: 这些植物赢得了争夺天空的战斗，解决了所有曾让

blocks.en_text: plants small and fragile and they took  over the planet in a few million years.
blocks.zh_text: 植物矮小脆弱的难题，并在几百万年里占领了整个星球。

blocks.en_text: Even today three trillion of  them cast their majestic shadows.
blocks.zh_text: 即使在今天，也有三万亿棵树投下它们雄伟的影子。

blocks.en_text: But we’ve barely covered half of it:  on top and below there are the crown
blocks.zh_text: 但我们才只讲了一半：上面和下面还有树冠

blocks.en_text: and the root system – one building  the tree from air, another mining
blocks.zh_text: 和根系——一个用空气建造树身，另一个用酸

blocks.en_text: minerals with acid and involved in complex  communications with fungi and other trees.
blocks.zh_text: 开采矿物质，还参与和真菌及其他树木的复杂交流。

blocks.en_text: There’s so much more to talk about, so we’re  already working on the next part - stay tuned!
blocks.zh_text: 还有太多可讲的，所以我们已经在做下一部分了——敬请期待！

blocks.en_text: Trees are truly incredible – but many  of our most beautiful forests are
blocks.zh_text: 树真的不可思议——但我们许多最美的森林正在

blocks.en_text: disappearing fast and we’re running  out of time to protect what’s left.
blocks.zh_text: 迅速消失，我们保护仅存森林的时间不多了。

blocks.en_text: That’s why we have partnered up with Planet Wild.
blocks.zh_text: 所以我们和Planet Wild合作了。

blocks.en_text: Planet Wild is a community-based  nature protection organization
blocks.zh_text: Planet Wild是一个社区型的自然保护组织，

blocks.en_text: that supports conservation  projects around the globe.
blocks.zh_text: 支持全球各地的保护项目。

blocks.en_text: Every month, their community of over 15,000  members funds a new mission to restore nature.
blocks.zh_text: 每个月，他们超过15000名成员的社区都会资助一项恢复自然的新任务。

blocks.en_text: We at kurzgesagt really value transparency.
blocks.zh_text: 我们kurzgesagt非常看重透明度。

blocks.en_text: That’s why we love that Planet Wild  documents all their missions in video
blocks.zh_text: 这就是我们喜欢 Planet Wild 的原因，他们把所有任务都拍成视频

blocks.en_text: reports right here on YouTube so you can  see what your contribution helped achieve.
blocks.zh_text: 报告，就发布在 YouTube 上，让你能看到自己的捐助促成了什么成果。

blocks.en_text: Take their underground forest mission in Tanzania:
blocks.zh_text: 看看他们在坦桑尼亚的地下森林任务：

blocks.en_text: While you think this desert is dead,  there’s actually life still here.
blocks.zh_text: 你可能以为这片沙漠毫无生机，其实这里依然有生命存在。

blocks.en_text: Beneath the surface, underground  forests are just waiting to grow.
blocks.zh_text: 在地表之下，地下森林正等着生长出来。

blocks.en_text: And with an ancient technique,  Planet Wild helped make that happen.
blocks.zh_text: Planet Wild 用一项古老的技术帮助实现了这一点。

blocks.en_text: If you would like to help our planet’s  ecosystems, consider joining Planet Wild.
blocks.zh_text: 如果你想帮助地球的生态系统，不妨考虑加入 Planet Wild。

blocks.en_text: You can give any amount that feels  right to you – every dollar counts.
blocks.zh_text: 你可以捐任何你觉得合适的金额——每一美元都很重要。

blocks.en_text: The first 100 people to sign up using our code
blocks.zh_text: 前100位用我们的优惠码注册的人

blocks.en_text: KURZGESAGT11 will get their  first month paid for by us!
blocks.zh_text: KURZGESAGT11，首月费用由我们来付！

blocks.en_text: Just scan the QR code or click  the link in the description.
blocks.zh_text: 只要扫描二维码，或点击简介里的链接就行。

blocks.en_text: Make a tree friend, and join the  Planet Wild community – today.
blocks.zh_text: 交一棵树做朋友，今天就加入 Planet Wild 社区吧。

blocks.en_text: If you want to see them in action first, check  out their underground forest mission here.
blocks.zh_text: 如果你想先看看他们的实际行动，可以点这里查看他们的地下森林任务。
